Content: So there is backstory to the ninja creamer. There is this brand called pacojet, they had a patent on whats called "pacotizing" its esentially sending a spinning blade down the beaker, that was the patent. Pacojets are AMAZING, almost every restaurant that serves dessert has a pacojet. Problem is they are over $7K new, around $3K used. We chefs LOVE the fact that we can make proper ice cream at home now. The mechanic is so simple so the ninja creamer does the exact same thing as a pacojet, a pacojet is just more engineered. You can make ice creams and sorbets at the level of noma, the french laundry etc. Teach yourself how to rocher/quenelle and you will be making the most beautiful ice creams at home

Author: @SvenskaIdioterna
Content:
So many of these things are completely useless. Two dishwashers? Really? How about just making sure you have enough stuff that you'll have a few left when you use the dishwasher? Or maybe you put EVERYTHING in there instead of handwashing some stuff, in which case it gets full in no time? A fridge you can see through? Like you said, just open the door. The energy loss isn't big if you don't look for a long time. There are other versions with similar space without the screen function that should be cheaper. The strainer is cool and since it's likely not expensive, it sounds like a decent buy, but does it add anything at all compared to a normal pasta strainer that doesn't tilt? You can place a regular strainer on the sink and just pour in pasta no issue. The only specialized strainer I got is a rice washing strainer since it's a bit of a chore to wash it and pour out the water from the bowl without letting the rice out too. 

The ice maker is absolutely useless, unless you regularly need tons of party ice or use the ice for something else. Get a fridge with an ice cube mode or just get some good ice cream mold, some are really good, that's more than enough for personal drinks, that should be obvious enough.

I also don't get the glasses. Why would someone want light glasses that easily topple, especially if you have cats? My glasses are all crystal. Heavy, sturdy, never falls, never moves unless I want it too. Doesn't break if I drop them either. I can see light glasses being a thing for a retired person with worsening strength, but not for most, especially not if you have cats. Mine like to sometimes dip their paws in my glasses or their entire heads, at least they don't fall over.

As for the roborock, it's definitely a game changer. I got the upgraded version of this, the saros 10r. Worth every bit of money. It cleans away cat litter from the floor a few times a day and keeps my floors overall looking pristine despite my cats. Had to fix a lot of things like cables and making sure it could get where it needs to go though, even building a ramp at a 5cm threshold. Wasn't cheap, especially not with everything you needed to get with it (cleaning solution, spare parts, things to organize the cables, materials to build a sturdy ramp etc), but it's great (just turned 30, got 70% of the money from various gifts). Got a dyson gen5 detect absolute for all spaces it can't get to, which is also the best vacuum I've ever had, just waiting for them to ship the floor dock since I don't want to wall mount, it was sold out sadly.

I just spray my toast with some water before toasting it in a normal toaster to give it a layer of water. Does help a bit.

As for the balmuda, everyone's saying not to buy their stuff anymore. For the lights under the bar, I would say to maybe look into seeing if Phillips has soft rope lights, getting channel diffusers for the current lights (though this means needing to cut the channels so they fit the length of the bar), or go with Govee for just this one item and use one of their rope lights (they now have several. I have Govee's string lights under my TV stand but installed them wrong. They face outwards instead of pointing down at the floor, but either way, the visible dots for every light is becoming annoying (and I dont have the patience or tools to cut the channel covers to fit the TV stand). It will look better if I just make it a solid light by using a rope light, because those are already diffused (and I think your bar will look a little better that way, too 😊). 

You've also convinced me that I might want to get a Ninja Creami. It seems way more efficent than the Cuisinart ice cream maker I have.
